summary: Zongsan Mou worked in philosophy and sinology. He studied at Peking University (1927–1933) and under Shili Xiong (~1932–1968). His academic career included posts at National Taiwan University, National Taiwan Normal University, Tunghai University, and the New Asia Institute (~1974–1995).

Zorya Nikolayevna Petrunicheva was an Indologist. She graduated in history from Moscow State University (~1943–1948) and worked as a researcher at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences in 1953.

Zsigmond Telegdi was a linguist and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at Budapest University of Jewish Studies, under Émile Benveniste, and at Eötvös Loránd University, where he later served as Professor of General Linguistics (1958–1979).

Zsuzsanna Renner works in Indology and history and archaeology. She earned an MA at Eötvös Loránd University (1978–1986). In 2017, she held posts as an honorary associate professor at Eötvös Loránd University and senior research fellow at Archaeolingua Foundation.

Zsóka Gelle is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Berzsenyi Dániel Teacher Training College, Eötvös Loránd University, and University of Vienna, and served as a Khyentse Fellow at Eötvös Loránd University and Budapest Centre for Buddhist Studies (2014–2016).
Zuicho Tachibana was a scholar of history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Kozui Otani (~1907–1914) and Edward Denison Ross (~1910–1912).

Zuiei Ito specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning doctorates at Waseda University and the University of Tokyo. He served as a professor in the Department of Buddhist Studies at Rissho University from 1980 to 2013.

Zuigan Goto worked in Buddhist studies. He studied at the Second Higher School, the University of Tokyo (1903–1906), and under Sokatsu Shaku (~1901–1914). In 1932, he served as president of Hanazono University.

Zuiho Yamaguchi was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Tokyo, École Pratique des Hautes Études, and under Rolf Alfred Stein and Jacques Bacot, he held professorships at the University of Tokyo (1970–1986) and Nagoya University (1986).

Zuiryu Nakamura was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Susumu Yamaguchi and Kenryu Tsukinowa, and served as a professor of Buddhist studies at Rissho University beginning in 1945.

Zygmunt Rysiewicz was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Lviv and under Jerzy Kuryłowicz, Louis Renou, Theodor Bloch, and Émile Benveniste. In 1949, he taught comparative linguistics at the University of Warsaw.
Gyurme tubten nyinje studied under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Shechen Gyaltsab.
Pad+ma la studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Dudjom Rinpoche.
Ármin Vámbéry was an Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar and linguist. He served as Professor of Oriental Languages at Eötvös Loránd University from 1865 and held a post at Nyugat.

Ènver Ahmedovič Makaev was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Moscow State University (~1933–1937) and Moscow State Linguistic University. He taught at Moscow State University (1938–1960) and served as a professor at the Institute of Linguistics (1954–1976).
Édouard Biot was a sinologist who studied under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat and Stanislas Julien.

Édouard Chavannes worked in sinology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure and Collège de France under Marquis d'Hervey de Saint-Denys and Maurice Jametel, later serving as professor at Collège de France (1893–1918).

Édouard Huber was a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at the Sorbonne and under Sylvain Lévi and Édouard Chavannes, later holding posts at École française d'Extrême-Orient (1901–1905) and the Sorbonne (1912–1914).
Édouard Lancereau was an Indologist who studied under Eugène Burnouf (~1845–1852). He held posts as a substitute teacher at Lycée Charlemagne and as a proofreader at the Imprimerie Nationale.
Édouard Specht was a sinologist who studied under Jean-Pierre-Guillaume Pauthier and Stanislas Julien. In 1892, he taught Chinese at the École Pratique des Hautes Études.
